title: Add variance analysis + automatic rerun policy for benchmark suites
author: Sana Farid
body:
Summary: This PR adds (1) variance summaries for benchmark runs (run-to-run variance, confidence bands) and (2) an automatic rerun policy when variance exceeds configured thresholds. This is a prerequisite for publishing latency/$ externally with defensible methodology language, and for keeping the internal pipeline from silently accepting noisy runs.

Motivation / context: We’ve had several cases where region-level noise (fleet contention, transient network jitter, autoscaling churn) made p95 latency jump 10–25% between otherwise identical runs. For the public benchmark effort we need: (a) a standard variance report attached to every suite, (b) a deterministic rerun trigger so results aren’t cherry-picked, and (c) a clear “unstable” state when the system cannot converge within bounded reruns.

What’s included: 1) Variance summary artifact: The suite runner now supports N repeated runs per (model, region, workload, config). We compute summary stats for key metrics: latency_p50, latency_p95, throughput_tok_s, cost_per_1m_tokens_usd, latency_per_dollar. For each metric we output: n, mean, std, cv (coefficient of variation), min/max, and a 95% confidence interval. CI method is bootstrap percentile over runs (default 2,000 resamples) with a deterministic RNG seed derived from suite_id so rebuilds are stable. Output is written to artifacts/<suite_id>/variance_summary.json and included in the aggregated result JSON.

2) Rerun policy + gating: We introduce a rerun policy that triggers extra repetitions when variance exceeds thresholds. Default policy: require at least 3 runs; if cv(latency_p95) > 0.08 OR ci_width(latency_p95)/mean(latency_p95) > 0.12, schedule up to 2 additional runs (max_total_runs=5). If after max_total_runs the suite is still above thresholds, mark the suite as unstable and exit non-zero (unless --allow-unstable is set). The intent is: internal pipelines fail fast; manual overrides are explicit; public-table generation can be configured to exclude unstable rows.

3) CLI + config: New flags: --repetitions, --bootstrap-resamples, --variance-thresholds (JSON), --max-total-runs, --allow-unstable. The region runner (PR #147) can pass these through consistently across regions.

4) Schema changes: Aggregated JSON now includes: variance_summary (per metric) and stability_status (stable|rerun_triggered|unstable). Note: the existing “flat” metrics remain unchanged to avoid breaking downstream consumers; the new fields are additive.

5) Tests + docs: Adds unit tests for bootstrap CI determinism, rerun trigger logic, and JSON schema validation. Updates README with “Interpreting variance_summary” and “When a suite is marked unstable”.

Implementation details: - CI computation: bootstrap percentile (2.5%, 97.5%) over run-level point estimates. Rationale: small N and non-normality observed in p95 distributions across runs.
- Determinism: uses numpy Generator(PCG64) seeded by a stable hash(suite_id + metric_name). Ensures confidence bands don’t change between retries when the run set is identical.
- Rerun scheduling: reruns are appended to the end of the suite execution plan to avoid starving other regions; backoff delay is applied when the previous run had elevated error rate.
- Guardrails: caps total benchmark time per suite by max_total_runs; prints a clear “why reran” message with the threshold it violated.

Out of scope / follow-ups: - We don’t yet compute run-to-run correlation with fleet-level GPU saturation metrics (would require wiring observability exports).
- We don’t attempt to “fix” noise; we only detect and report it.

Risk / compatibility: Low. Changes are additive to output schema, but downstream tools that strictly validate unknown keys should be checked. I updated the internal schema validator in this PR; if you have external consumers pinning a strict schema, use --legacy-output to strip variance fields (added here as a safety valve).

Checklist: - [x] Additive schema change only (no renames/removals)
- [x] Deterministic CI bands given identical runs
- [x] Rerun policy bounded (max_total_runs)
- [x] Unit tests for rerun logic + CI determinism
- [x] Docs updated

How to test locally: 1) python -m benchmark_lab.run_suite --suite configs/suites/chat_baseline.yaml --region us-east-1 --repetitions 3 2) Inspect artifacts/<suite_id>/variance_summary.json 3) Force noise thresholds: --variance-thresholds '{"latency_p95": {"cv": 0.0}}' and confirm rerun triggers and suite marks unstable at max_total_runs.

Notes for public benchmark project: This is intended to support methodology language like “results reflect median across repeated runs; we report 95% confidence bands across runs; rows exceeding variance thresholds are rerun up to a fixed limit and flagged unstable if not converged.”
commits: benchmark: add VarianceSummary dataclass + JSON serialization
runner: implement bootstrap CI + determinism seed plumbing
policy: add rerun trigger thresholds + stability_status
tests: add variance + rerun unit tests; update schema validator
docs: update README with variance interpretation + unstable behavior
changed_files: benchmark_lab/io/output_schema.py: additive schema + legacy strip mode
review_conversation: Claire Dubois: Can you clarify why we’re using bootstrap percentile vs t-interval? With N=3 the CI can be misleading either way; want us to be explicit about method.

Sana Farid (author): Added rationale in README + inline docstring. Bootstrap percentile behaves better with the heavy-tailed p95 behavior we’re seeing; also deterministic with seeded resampling. We should still call out that the band is across repeated runs (not per-request).
Rina Kobayashi: Reruns at max_total_runs=5 could extend region windows. Do we have a hard cap per suite and a way to see why reruns happened without digging into logs?
Sana Farid (author): Yes—max_total_runs is enforced; also printing a structured “RERUN_TRIGGER” line with violated threshold + current stats. Added it to the aggregated JSON under rerun_reasons[].
Neha Kapoor: For SRE safety, can we ensure unstable suites fail by default in automation, but allow manual override for ad-hoc exploration?
Sana Farid (author): Default is exit non-zero when unstable; --allow-unstable will keep exit 0 but sets stability_status=unstable. CI jobs should keep default; exploratory runs can override.
Caleb Johnson: CI width calculation: are we using (hi-lo)/mean? For near-zero metrics that could blow up.
Sana Farid (author): Yes (hi-lo)/mean for now; added a small epsilon guard and we only apply gating thresholds to latency/throughput/cost/latency_per_dollar (no near-zero metrics).
Jonas Weber: Please ensure we don’t accidentally claim “statistical significance” anywhere. This should be variance reporting, not hypothesis testing.

Sana Farid (author): Agreed. No significance language added. README and output fields are named “confidence_interval” but described as bootstrap band across runs; no p-values or claims of significance.
Claire Dubois: Looks good after the rerun_reasons addition + README clarification. Approved.
Rina Kobayashi: Approved (please follow up with a small change in #147 to set repetitions=3 by default for public suites).
